There is no power and no strength except by Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and we do not worship except Him. To Him belongs all favor, grace, and good praise. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, making our religion sincerely for Him, even if the disbelievers dislike it.

duas.context: There is No Partner for Allah, and To Him Belongs All Things
duas.arabic: لاَ إِلَـهَ إِلاَّ اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيْكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيْرُ
duas.transliteration: la ilaha illa allah wahdahu la sharika lah. lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir
duas.text: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs dominion and praise, and He is over all things competent.

duas.context: Al-Ikhlas
duas.arabic: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (1) ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ (2) لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ (3) وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ (4)
duas.transliteration: qul huwa allahu ahad (1) allahu samad (2) lam yalid wa lam yulad (3) wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad (4)
duas.text: Say, "He is Allah , [who is] One, (1) Allah , the Eternal Refuge. (2) He neither begets nor is born, (3) Nor is there to Him any equivalent." (4)
duas.source: HR. Abu Dawud No. 1523 and an-Nasa'i No. 1337. Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir said that the chain of this hadith is hasan

duas.context: Al-Falaq
duas.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ (1) مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ (2) وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ (3) وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ (4) وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ (5)
duas.transliteration: qul a'udhu birabbil-falaq (1) min sharri ma khalaq (2) wa min sharri ghasiqin idha waqab (3) wa min sharri naffathati fil-'uqad (4) wa min sharri hasidin idha hasad (5)
duas.text: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak (1) From the evil of that which He created (2) And from the evil of darkness when it settles (3) And from the evil of the blowers in knots (4) And from the evil of an envier when he envies." (5)
duas.source: HR. Abu Dawud No. 1523 and an-Nasa'i No. 1337. Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir said that the chain of this hadith is hasan

duas.context: An-Nas
duas.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ (1) مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ (2) إِلَٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ (3) مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ (4) ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ (5) مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ (6)
duas.transliteration: qul a'udhu birabbin-nas (1) malikin-nas (2) ilahin-nas (3) min sharri al-waswasi al-khannas (4) alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudurin-nas (5) mina al-jinnati wan-nas (6)
duas.text: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, (1) The King of mankind. (2) The God of mankind, (3) From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, (4) Who whispers in the breasts of mankind, (5) Of the jinn and mankind." (6)
duas.source: HR. Abu Dawud No. 1523 and an-Nasa'i No. 1337. Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir said that the chain of this hadith is hasan

duas.context: Supplication for Beneficial Knowledge, Good Provision, and Accepted Deeds
duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّى أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا وَعَمَلاً مُتَقَبَّلاً
duas.transliteration: allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan tayyiban, wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan
duas.text: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and accepted deeds.
duas.source: HR. Ibn Majah No. 925 and Ahmad 6: 305, 322. Al-Hafiz Abu Tahir said that this hadith is sahih

duas.context: Entering the Evening in the Kingdom of Allah and Seeking His Protection
duas.arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ للهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ للهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا، وَأَعُوذُبِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا، رَبِّ أَعُوذُبِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُبِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
duas.transliteration: amsayna wa amsal-mulku lillahi wal-hamdu lillahi, la ilaha illa allah wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahu al-mulku wa lahu al-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir. rabbi as'aluka khayra ma fi hadhihil-laylah wa khayra ma ba'daha, wa a'udhu bika min sharri ma fi hadhihil-laylah wa sharri ma ba'daha. rabbi a'udhu bika mina al-kasali wa su'il-kibar. rabbi a'udhu bika min 'adhabin fin-nar wa 'adhabin fil-qabr
duas.text: We have entered the evening and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him is praise, and He is over all things competent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evil of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the Fire and the punishment of the grave.
duas.source: HR. Muslim No. 2723 (75), Abu Dawud No. 5071, and at-Tirmidzi 3390, sahih from Abdullah Ibn Mas'ud

duas.context: Entering the Evening by Seeking Allah's Mercy
duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا،وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيْرُ
duas.transliteration: allahumma bika amsayna, wa bika asbahna, wa bika nahya, wa bika namutu wa ilayka al-masir
duas.text: O Allah, by Your grace and help we have entered the evening, and by Your grace and help we enter the morning. By Your grace and help we live and by Your will we die. And to You is the final return (of all creatures).
duas.source: HR. al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad No. 1199, this wording is the wording of al-Bukhari at-Tirmidzi No. 3391, Abu Dawud No. 5068, Ahmad 11/354, Ibn Majah No. 3868

duas.context: Prayer for Health and Protection
duas.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِيْ فِيْ بَدَنِيْ ، اَللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِيْ فِيْ سَمْعِيْ ، اَللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِيْ فِيْ بَصَرِيْ ، لَا إِلَـهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ ، اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكُفْرِوَالْفَقْرِ ، وَأَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ ، لَا إِلَـهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
duas.transliteration: allahumma 'afini fi badani, allahumma 'afini fi sam'i, allahumma 'afini fi basari, la ilaha illa anta. allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-kufri wal-faqr, allahumma inni a'udhu bika min 'adhabil-qabr, la ilaha illa anta
duas.text: O Allah, protect my body (from illness and from what I do not want). O Allah, protect my hearing (from illness and disobedience or from what I do not want). O Allah, protect my sight, there is no deity worthy of worship except You. O Allah, indeed I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty. I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, there is no deity worthy of worship except You.
duas.source: HR. al-Bukhari in Sahih al-Adab al-Mufrad No. 701, Abu Dawud No. 5090, Ahmad V/42, hasan

duas.context: Prayer for Safety in This World and the Hereafter
duas.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَاْلآخِرَةِ، اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِيْنِيْ وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِيْ وَمَالِيْ اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِى وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِى. اَللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْنِيْ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ، وَمِنْ خَلْفِيْ، وَعَنْ يَمِيْنِيْ وَعَنْ شِمَالِيْ، وَمِنْ فَوْقِيْ، وَأَعُوْذُ بِعَظَمَتِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِيْ
duas.transliteration: allahumma inni as'alukal-'afwa wal-'afiyah fid-dunya wal-akhirah. allahumma inni as'alukal-'afwa wal-'afiyah fi dini wa dunyaya wa ahli wa mali. allahummastur 'awrati wa amin raw'ati. allahummahfadhni min bayni yadayya wa min khalfi wa 'an yamini wa 'an shimali wa min fawqi wa a'udhu bi 'adhamatika an ughtala min tahti
duas.text: O Allah, indeed I ask You for well-being and safety in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, indeed I ask You for well-being and safety in my religion, my world, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my flaws (faults and things that are not appropriate for others to see) and calm me from fear. O Allah, protect me from the front, behind, right, left and above me. I seek refuge in Your greatness, so that I am not snatched from below me (by snakes or swallowed by the earth, etc., which would cause me to fall).
duas.source: HR. al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad No. 1200, Abu Dawud No. 5074, an-Nasa'i VII/282, Ibn Majah No. 3871, al-Hakim 1/517-518, and others from Ibn Umar radhiyallahu 'anhuma

duas.context: Prayer for Seeking Protection from the Whispers of Satan
duas.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَاْلأَرْضِ، رَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيْكَهُ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَـهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ، أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ نَفْسِيْ، وَمِنْ شَرِّ الشَّيْطَانِ وَشِرْكِهِ، وَأَنْ أَقْتَرِفَ عَلَى نَفْسِيْ سُوْءًا أَوْ أَجُرَّهُ إِلَى مُسْلِمٍ
duas.transliteration: allahumma 'alimal-ghaybi wash-shahadati, fatiras-samawati wal-ard, rabbakulli shayin wa malikahu. ashhadu alla ilaha illa anta, a'udhu bika min sharri nafsi, wa min sharri ash-shaytani wa shirkih. wa an aqtarifa 'ala nafsi su'an aw ajurrahu ila muslim
duas.text: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord of all things and their Sovereign. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself, Satan and his soldiers (temptations to commit shirk against Allah), and I (seek refuge in You) from committing evil against myself or dragging it to a Muslim.
duas.source: HR. al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad No. 1202, at-Tirmidzi No. 3392 and Abu Dawud No. 5067

duas.context: Remembrance to Be Protected from All Dangers
duas.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِى لاَ يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَىْءٌ فِى الأَرْضِ وَلاَ فِى السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
duas.transliteration: bismillahilladhi la yadurru ma'asmihi shay'un fil-ardi wa la fis-sama' wa huwas-sami'ul-'alim
duas.text: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing in the earth or the heavens can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
duas.source: HR. at-Tirmidzi No. 3388, Abu Dawud No. 5088, Ibn Majah No. 3869, al-Hakim 1/514, and Ahmad No. 446 and 474

duas.context: Declaration of Contentment with Allah, Islam, and the Prophet Muhammad sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam
duas.arabic: رَضِيْتُ بِاللهِ رَبًّا، وَبِاْلإِسْلاَمِ دِيْنًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَبِيًّا
duas.transliteration: raditu billahi rabba, wa bil-islami dina, wa bi-muhammadin sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallama nabiyya
duas.text: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, Islam as my religion, and Muhammad, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, as my Prophet.
duas.source: HR. Ahmad IV/337, Abu Dawud No. 5072, at-Tirmidzi No. 3389, Ibn Majah No. 3870, an-Nasa'i in 'Amalul Yaum wal Lailah No. 4 and Ibnus Sunni No. 68

duas.context: Asking for Guidance from Allah
duas.arabic: يَا حَيُّ يَا قَيُّوْمُ بِرَحْمَتِكَ أَسْتَغِيْثُ، وَأَصْلِحْ لِيْ شَأْنِيْ كُلَّهُ وَلاَ تَكِلْنِيْ إِلَى نَفْسِيْ طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ أَبَدًا
duas.transliteration: ya hayyu ya qayyum, bi-rahmatika astaghith, wa aslih li sha'ni kullahu wa la takilni ila nafsi tarfata 'aynin abada
duas.text: O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, by Your mercy I seek help, rectify all my affairs and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.
duas.source: HR. an-Nasa'i in 'Amalul Yaum wal Lailah No. 575, and al-Hakim 1/545, see Sahih at-Targhib wat Tarhib 1/417 No. 661, As-Sahihah No. 227, hasan

duas.context: Entering the Evening on the Natural Disposition of Islam
duas.arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ اْلإِسْلاَمِ وَعَلَى كَلِمَةِ اْلإِخْلاَصِ، وَعَلَى دِيْنِ نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَعَلَى مِلَّةِ أَبِيْنَا إِبْرَاهِيْمَ، حَنِيْفًا مُسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِيْنَ
duas.transliteration: amsayna 'ala fitratil-islam wa 'ala kalimatil-ikhlas, wa 'ala dini nabiyyina muhammadin sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, wa 'ala millati abina ibrahima hanifan musliman wa ma kana minal-mushrikin
duas.text: In the evening we are upon the fitrah of Islam, the word of sincerity (the testimony of faith), the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and the religion of our father Abraham, who stood upon the straight path, a Muslim, and was not among the polytheists.
duas.source: HR. Ahmad III/406, 407, ad-Darimi II/292 and Ibnus Sunni in Amalul Yaum wal Lailah No. 34, Mishkat al-Masabih No. 2415, Sahih al-Jami' as-Saghir No. 4674, sahih

duas.context: Reciting Praise to Allah
duas.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ عَدَدَ خَلْقَهِ وَرِضَى نَفْسِهِ وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ
duas.transliteration: subhanallahi wa bihamdihi 'adada khalqihi wa rida nafsihi wa zinata 'arshihi wa midada kalimatihi
duas.text: Glory be to Allah, as many as His creations, Glory be to Allah as much as His pleasure, Glory be to Allah as much as the weight of His Throne, and as much as the ink of His written words.
duas.source: HR. Muslim No. 2726. Sharh Muslim XVII/44. From Juwairiyah bint al-Harith radhiyallahu 'anha

duas.context: Daily Praise (Tasbih and Alhamdulillah)
duas.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
duas.transliteration: subhanallahi wa bihamdihi
duas.text: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him.
duas.source: HR. Muslim No. 2691 and No. 2692, from Abu Hurairah radhiyallahu 'anhu Sharh Muslim XVII/17-18, Sahih at-Targhib wat Tarhib 1/413 No. 653

duas.context: Seeking Forgiveness 100 Times a Day
duas.arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ الله وَأَتُوْبُ إِلَيْهِ
duas.transliteration: astaghfirullah wa atubu ilayh
duas.text: I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.
duas.source: HR. al-Bukhari/Fat-hul Baari XI/101 and Muslim No. 2702

duas.context: Ayatul Kursi
duas.arabic: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
duas.transliteration: allahu la ilaha illa huwa, al-hayyul-qayyum. la ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm. lahu ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ard. man dhal-ladhi yashfa'u 'indahu illa bi-idhnihi. ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim wa ma khalfahum. wa la yuhituna bishay'in min 'ilmihi illa bima sha'. wa si'a kursiyyuhu as-samawati wal-ard. wa la ya'udu-hu hifdhuhuma. wa huwa al-'aliyyul-'azim
duas.text: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most Hight, the Most Great.

duas.context: Upon Entering The Morning by Asking for Protection from Allah
duas.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لاَ إِلَـهَ إِلاَّ اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيْكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيْرُ. رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِيْ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهُ، وَأَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِيْ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ، رَبِّ أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوْءِ الْكِبَرِ، رَبِّ أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
duas.transliteration: asbahna wa asbahal-mulku lillahi, wal-hamdu lillahi, la ilaha illa allah wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahu al-mulku wa lahu al-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir. rabbi as'aluka khayra ma fi hadha al-yawm wa khayra ma ba'dahu, wa a'udhu bika min sharri ma fi hadha al-yawm wa sharri ma ba'dahu. rabbi a'udhu bika mina al-kasali wa su'il-kibar. rabbi a'udhu bika min 'adhabin fin-nar wa 'adhabin fil-qabr
duas.text: We have entered the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, He has no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him is praise, and He is over all things competent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evil of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the Fire and the punishment of the grave.
duas.source: HR. Muslim No. 2723 (75), Abu Dawud No. 5071, and at-Tirmidzi 3390, sahih from Abdullah Ibn Mas'ud

duas.context: Upon Entering The Morning with The Grace of Allah
duas.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوْتُ وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُوْرُ
duas.transliteration: allahumma bika asbahna, wa bika amsayna, wa bika nahya, wa bika namutu wa ilaykan-nushur
duas.text: O Allah, with Your grace and help we enter the morning, and with Your grace and help we enter the evening. By Your grace and will we live and by Your grace and will we die. And to You is the resurrection (for all creatures).
duas.source: HR. al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad No. 1199, this wording is the wording of al-Bukhari, at-Tirmidzi No. 3391, Abu Dawud No. 5068, Ahmad 11/354, Ibn Majah No. 3868

duas.context: Entering The Morning Upon The Natural Religion of Islam
duas.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ اْلإِسْلاَمِ وَعَلَى كَلِمَةِ اْلإِخْلاَصِ، وَعَلَى دِيْنِ نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَعَلَى مِلَّةِ أَبِيْنَا إِبْرَاهِيْمَ، حَنِيْفًا مُسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِيْنَ
duas.transliteration: asbahna 'ala fitratil-islam wa 'ala kalimatil-ikhlas, wa 'ala dini nabiyyina muhammadin sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, wa 'ala millati abina ibrahima hanifan musliman wa ma kana minal-mushrikin
duas.text: In the morning we are upon the fitrah of Islam, the word of sincerity (the testimony of faith), the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and the religion of our father Abraham, who stood upon the straight path, a Muslim, and was not among the polytheists.
duas.source: HR. Ahmad III/406, 407, ad-Darimi II/292 and Ibnus Sunni in Amalul Yaum wal Lailah No. 34, Mishkat al-Masabih No. 2415, Sahih al-Jami' as-Saghir No. 4674, sahih

duas.context: Dua To Make Heart Firm Upon Deen #1
duas.arabic: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِى عَلَى دِينِكَ
duas.transliteration: ya muqallibal-qulubi thabbit qalbi 'ala dinik
duas.text: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.

duas.context: Dua To Make Heart Firm Upon Deen #2
duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ مُصَرِّفَ الْقُلُوبِ صَرِّفْ قُلُوبَنَا عَلَى طَاعَتِكَ
duas.transliteration: allahumma musarrifal-qulubi sarrif qulubana 'ala ta'atik
duas.text: O Allah! Controller of the hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience.

duas.context: Dua To Make Heart Firm Upon Deen #3
duas.arabic: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا
duas.transliteration: rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana
duas.text: O our Lord, do not make our hearts incline to error after You have guided us.

duas.context: Dua To Seek Refuge Against The Loss Of Pleasure
duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّى أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ زَوَالِ نِعْمَتِكَ وَتَحَوُّلِ عَافِيَتِكَ وَفُجَاءَةِ نِقْمَتِكَ وَجَمِيعِ سَخَطِكَ
duas.transliteration: allahumma inni a'udhu bika min zawali ni'matik, wa tahawwuli 'afiyatik, wa fuja'ati niqmatik, wa jami'i sakhatik
duas.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the loss of the pleasures that You have bestowed, from changes in the health that You have bestowed, from Your sudden torment, and from all Your wrath.

duas.context: Dua To Resist Affliction
duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ جَهْدِ البَلاَءِ ، وَدَرَكِ الشَّقَاءِ ، وَسُوءِ القَضَاءِ ، وَشَمَاتَةِ الأَعْدَاء
duas.transliteration: allahumma inni a'udhu bika min jahdil-bala', wa darakish-shaqa', wa su'il-qada', wa shamatatil-a'da'
duas.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from severe calamity, being overtaken by misery, evil destiny, and the triumphant mockery of enemies.

duas.context: Dua When Getting Good News
duas.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِى بِنِعْمَتِهِ تَتِمُّ الصَّالِحَاتُ
duas.transliteration: alhamdu lillahi alladhi bini'matihi tattimmu assalihat
duas.text: Praise be to Allah, by whose grace goodness is perfected.
duas.source: HR. Ibn Majah in the Sunan, No. 3803 and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/499)
